Reader main loop, version checking and error reporting beyond single segment pacing and pipe helpers.
Scale operations descriptor layout and per variant behavior beyond selection by name.
Grace period polling, conditional synchronization and callback barrier implementations behind the operations descriptor.
Free list initialization, pool refill policy and retired list concurrency beyond allocation, freeing and sweep.
Bodies of forward progress, barrier, boost, stall, fake writer, no callback, statistics and force quiescence workers.

findings.text: Scale startup selects one operations descriptor by matching a requested name against a table that includes regular, sleepable and task based variants, optionally runs its initializer, captures grace thread timing when available, derives realized thread counts, announces parameters, then brings up reader, expedited and writer workers with per writer measurement storage and optional asynchronous free lists before reporting success or unwinding through a common cleanup path.

Selection requires an exact name match and otherwise reports the failure, enumerates available names and aborts with no active descriptor. Asynchronous mode requires a positive queue bound and per writer queue storage, and every worker and measurement allocation must succeed, otherwise startup fails after cleanup.

Startup moves from argument gating through selection and optional initialization into ordered worker creation with readers required to signal readiness before expedited and writer creation, ending in either a running test or an unwind that ends initialization, invokes cleanup and conditionally powers off when a timed shutdown was requested.

Low byte reader extensions use values one, two, four, eight, sixteen, thirty two, sixty four and one hundred twenty eight for bottom half suppression, interrupt suppression, preemption suppression, nested bottom half entry, nested scheduler entry, first nested entry, second nested entry and timer mediated transfer respectively.

First sleepable index starts at bit eight and second at bit sixteen, each mask covering eight bits in that position, with eight defined low bits, at most seven extension iterations and at most ten segments per record, where the extendable set combines the first five low bits while omitting timer transfer and the all bits set additionally includes both nested entries and both index masks.
Pipe length is ten, the reusable element pool holds ten times that many entries, and the per stage histogram has one more slot than the pipe length.

Writer phase codes assign RTWS_FIXED_DELAY zero, RTWS_DELAY one, RTWS_REPLACE two, RTWS_DEF_FREE three, RTWS_EXP_SYNC four, RTWS_COND_GET five, RTWS_COND_GET_FULL six, RTWS_COND_GET_EXP seven, RTWS_COND_GET_EXP_FULL eight, RTWS_COND_SYNC nine, RTWS_COND_SYNC_FULL ten, RTWS_COND_SYNC_EXP eleven, RTWS_COND_SYNC_EXP_FULL twelve, RTWS_POLL_GET thirteen, RTWS_POLL_GET_FULL fourteen, RTWS_POLL_GET_EXP fifteen, RTWS_POLL_GET_EXP_FULL sixteen, RTWS_POLL_WAIT seventeen, RTWS_POLL_WAIT_FULL eighteen, RTWS_POLL_WAIT_EXP nineteen, RTWS_POLL_WAIT_EXP_FULL twenty, RTWS_SYNC twenty one, RTWS_STUTTER twenty two and RTWS_STOPPING twenty three, mirrored by a name table in identical order.
Default torture selector designates the regular variant.
Log prefix helper is identity over its format argument.

Reader validation record carries the reader loop count, the assigned checker identity, the checker loop count, a readiness flag and a back link to the assigning record, placed to avoid cross node false sharing.
Torture element bundles a callback header, a pipe stage counter, a free list link, a memory ordering test flag and an optional pointer to a reader validation record.

Read segment diagnostic record stores a state code, three delay magnitudes at different granularities, a preemption marker, start and end processor identities, start and end grace sequence values and a timestamp, with a small static array retaining recent erroneous segments plus counters for recorded errors, active segments and preemption observations.

Operations descriptor groups lifecycle hooks, reader entry and timing controls, grace observation and waiting primitives in normal and expedited as well as single and full sequence forms, callback and barrier handling, force and statistics diagnostics, boost and stall introspection and capability flags with a textual name, with a single global pointer selecting the active descriptor.

Allocation and freeing serialize free list removal and insertion under a bottom half disabled spin critical section that also guards outcome accounting, with empty list reported as allocation failure.
Boost start time updates are serialized by a dedicated mutex, while the processor online query disables preemption around its per processor state inspection.
Pipe stage counters rely on exclusive writer ownership rather than additional locking.

Allocator removes the first free element when available and otherwise records a miss and returns absence, while the releaser appends to the tail and records a free, with total allocation attempts also counted.
Pipe maintenance optionally enqueues a retired element then scans the retired list advancing each element one stage and reclaiming those that reach the terminal stage.

Single stage advancement first publishes any attached reader check as ready after detaching it, clamps overrun counts to the pipe bound, records histogram membership for the prior stage, increments the stage and clears the ordering test flag exactly when the terminal stage is reached to signal reclaimability.

Normal reader entry acquires protection and reports a constant handle that release ignores, while nesting depth prefers a dedicated preemptible depth query when configured, otherwise extracts the preemption count field when available, and otherwise reports unavailability.

Reader pacing is skipped entirely while forward progress callbacks request no delay, otherwise it probabilistically injects a rare long stall that samples grace progress around the stall and emits a diagnostic trace, an occasional short stall and an occasional voluntary schedule that only acts as a quiescent point when preemptible, with long stalls shortened when executed with hardware or software interrupt context outstanding.

Shared gate reports that lock state checks are vacuous when debugging is inactive and reports not held when observation is inactive or the current processor is logically offline, with debugging considered active only after scheduler activation with global debug locks enabled and no current lockdep recursion.

Bottom half protection query reflects soft interrupt or disabled interrupt state and scheduler protection query reflects scheduler lock ownership or non preemptible state after the shared gate, with a torture helper combining both as a not held test.

Processor online query for lock validation returns affirmative during non maskable interrupt handling or before full scheduler activation and otherwise inspects online state or offline lock contention without tracing or preemption.
Trace timestamp helper converts a local trace clock to microsecond granularity in one configuration and yields zero in the other.
Torture read trace hook forwards its name, callback, timing and sequence arguments to the tracing layer when enabled and is otherwise a no operation.
Writer phase name resolution reads the current phase once and returns the corresponding table entry or a placeholder when the value lies outside the table.
Barrier test coordination tracks registered versus invoked callback counts together with a phase flag and a wait queue pointer.
Shutdown is considered imminent during the final thirty seconds before the configured deadline, with boost scheduling state held alongside.

Torture harness retains handles for writer, readers, fake writers, up down, no callback offload, statistics, force quiescence, per processor boost, stall, forward progress, barrier callback, barrier, read exit and preempt workers plus realized counts for readers, fake writers and offload threads.

Published pointer and monotonic version identify the current element from a fixed pool, with a retired list, start sequence, error and progress counters and offload transition tallies capturing test outcome.

Failed startup always runs cleanup and, when a timed shutdown was armed, additionally warns unless built as a module and then powers off, so initialization failure can terminate the machine in that configuration.

Intentional long reader stalls prolong grace periods by design and rely on shortened stalls under interrupt context to avoid breaching bottom half limits, so mistuned delays or ignored forward progress bypass can distort timing or trigger latency complaints.

Reclamation walks and mutates the retired list while freeing terminal elements and assumes single threaded stage updates, so concurrent writers or premature reuse would corrupt counts and list membership.
Online determination treats offline lock contention as online to suppress warnings, which can hide genuine offline misuse when the lock is held by another processor.
